messages:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — elevated 5xx rate across control-plane endpoints (auth, org-lookup, billing). Seen from 02:01 UTC. Spike in 502/504 and timeouts. Pager: https://pager.redwood/INC-20260315-01 :rotating_light:

Emma (SRE): acked. I'm oncall — investigating. first look at traces and gateway logs.

Priya (Eng): joining. I'm pulling auth and org-lookup traces now. seeing a big tail on auth verify calls. :eyes:

Zoe (Support): getting customer reports — several tenants have API requests failing with 502s. Support is fielding inbound tickets and escalating. Customers affected include two dedicated accounts on us-east-1.

Emma (SRE): high-level: control-plane is returning 502s because it can't reach upstream auth/org services; billing calls also timing out. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/controlplane/errors?since=02:00 UTC.

Priya (Eng): quick reproduction (from my laptop):
```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/organizations/lookup?id=acct_123"
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
> X-Request-Id: rqd-ef12-34
{"error":"upstream_auth_unavailable","code":502}
```

Priya (Eng): stack traces show upstream auth-db connection timeouts (pg pool exhausted) and a surge in org-lookup fanout. Likely multi-dep pressure rather than one-off code bug.

Alex (Platform): I'm checking k8s and infra autoscaling. `kubectl get pods -n control-plane` shows a couple of auth pods in CrashLoopBackOff and frequent restarts.

Emma (SRE): logs snippet from gateway at 02:07 UTC: 
```
W 02:07:12 gateway.go:432 request=abcd err="upstream timeout" upstream=/controlplane/auth/verify status=504
E 02:07:13 gateway.go:439 request=abce err="upstream 502" upstream=/controlplane/org/lookup status=502
```

Priya (Eng): immediate mitigations I can try now: 1) increase auth DB pool size (configmap) 2) scale auth deployment +2 replicas 3) enable cached org-lookup fallback. which one do we want first?

Emma (SRE): do them in order: scale + enable fallback. scaling is safest. I'll trigger scale and watch.

Alex (Platform): scaling auth to 4 -> 6 replicas now. command: `kubectl scale deployment/auth --replicas=6 -n control-plane` (started). :white_check_mark:

Deploy Bot: Started roll: scale deployment/auth -> 6 replicas (user Alex). Roll ID: roll-1901234567-1.

Priya (Eng): also patching configmap to increase pg pool from 50 -> 100 (temp). applying now.

Emma (SRE): enabling org-lookup cached fallback. runbook: https://runbook.redwood/controlplane/fallbacks. Patch flag: `ENABLE_ORG_CACHED_FALLBACK=true`. Applying via k8s env update.

Alex (Platform): doing the env update now: `kubectl set env deployment/control-plane ENABLE_ORG_CACHED_FALLBACK=true -n control-plane`.

Emma (SRE): monitoring metrics. error rate dropped ~40% in the 30s after scale + fallback. still seeing intermittent 502s for billing calls.

Zoe (Support): pinging affected customers with a status update: "We're aware of intermittent 502/504s; mitigation in progress. ETA ~15–30m for fuller resolution." Will escalate accounts flagged as P0.

Priya (Eng): billing timeouts appear to be a separate downstream (billing-queue) — added a temporary retry/backoff around billing calls in control-plane to reduce immediate failures. patching now (hotfix).

Emma (SRE): hotfix applied. error rate trending down, latency on /auth/verify back to normal for most requests. :thumbsup:

Priya (Eng): verifying DB metrics: connection pool usage dropped after scale and pool increase. looks like pool exhaustion was the main trigger.

Emma (SRE): next steps: open incident ticket, record timeline, assign postmortem. Who takes lead on the runbook and action items?

Alex (Platform): I'll own the mitigation writeup and do a config audit for default pool sizes.

Zoe (Support): I'll follow up with customers once we have stable green. Draft status note in the ticket and send targeted emails for the two dedicated customers.

PagerDuty Bot: Note: Escalate to SEV2 if errors persist beyond 45m.

Emma (SRE): handing off live watch to Alex for the overnight window. I'm stepping off after 20m of stable green. Alex, I left a checklist in the incident ticket: `INC-20260315-01`.

Alex (Platform): taking watch. I'll keep the scaling and fallback in place until config changes are validated in the morning. Also filing infra ticket to increase DB capacity for auth-primary.

Priya (Eng): followups for postmortem: - determine why pool was sized low for spike scenarios - add autoscaling policy tied to auth latency - add defensive rate-limits on org-lookup fanout - ensure caching is fast-fail safe.

Emma (SRE): agreed. tagging owners and adding to timeline. Good job team — fewer customer errors now but keep eyes on it. :eyes: :white_check_mark:

Deploy Bot: Roll complete: roll-1901234567-1 -> scale + config changes succeeded.

Alex (Platform): final note before assuming watch: created JIRA RED-7812 for followups and postmortem; linking incident ticket and runbook. Handoff: @Priya and @Zoe added as stakeholders.

Zoe (Support): I'll keep support queue updates going. If anything spikes back up I'll re-open pager.

Emma (SRE): leaving channel — thanks all. :wave:

Alex (Platform): oncall watch started.

[end of thread]
